findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the beginning of the inspection there was no a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) available at the facility. One was called and arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that there is a CFPM available at all times that the kitchen is in use in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Multiple items in the walk in cooler were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-50F. The PIC was shown and the TCS items discarded to correct the violations. Items discarded included corned beef, coleslaw, ham, cheese, pizza, marinara, cheese sauce, chicken breast, and BBQ pulled pork. Ensure that the cold old int in the facility is maintained at correct temperatures at all times. This violation is for the foods being out of safe temperature ranges only. Refer to line item #33 for the cooler.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

A half gallon of milk was observed in the server cooler partially used and without a date marking. When asked, staff indicated that it was opened “a couple days ago”. Education was conducted and a date marking added to the container to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods in the facility are properly dated once they are prepared or the packaging is opened.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The walk in cooler was observed to be holding foods with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-50F. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the cooler repaired prior to the follow up in 10 days. This violation is for the cooler not functioning correctly.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Food Handler Certificates were unavailable for multiple employees on staff during today’s inspection. Ensure all food service staff obtain a Food Handler’s certificate to be made available during future inspections. Inspector provided guidance on where to find ANSI-approved Food Handler’s certificate Courses.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

None of the CFPMs employed by the facility currently had an allergen training certificate available during the inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that the CFPMs complete the training and maintain a copy of the certificates at the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection a CFPM certificate was not available at the facility. The PIC indicated that several employees had taken the course/test but were unable to provide certificates for verification. The situation was discussed and options for getting the certificates from ServeSafe given. Ensure that certificates are available for the CFPMs/PICs at the facility prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) If used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The blade of the can opener was observed soiled with dry food debris. When asked the PIC indicated that it had not been used that day, indicating that it was not properly cleaned the day before. Education was conducted and the PIC moved the can opener to dish to remedy the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned correctly and often.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be thawed: (A-E) Using an approved method. 

A log of ground beef is observed in standing water in a sink. When asked an employee indicated that it was thawing in cold water for later service. This is not an approved method. The PIC was consulted and education conducted. Ensure that the TCS foods are thawed in a safe manner in the facility. The log was prepared during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Multiple ladles stored hanging at the west side of the kitchen were observed soiled with food debris. The PIC indicated that it was likely caused by the pizza racks being stored on the shelf above. This is likely, but the food contact surfaces must be protected from contamination prior to use. Moving the ladles or the racks are both viable options to remedy the situation. The contaminated ladles were moved to dish for cleaning to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are protected from contamination prior to use in the facility.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
(REEPAT) 410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Food Handler Certificates were unavailable for multiple employees on staff during today’s inspection. Ensure all food service staff obtain a Food Handler’s certificate to be made available during future inspections. Inspector provided guidance on where to find ANSI-approved Food Handler’s certificate Courses.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to produce employee reporting agreements. Inspector gave the PIC a blank employee reporting agreement. Have employees review and sign agreement to maintain on file for future inspections. Inspector will return on 12/19/25 to check for compliance.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple food handlers wash their hands, and turn off the faucet without a barrier. CORRECTED- education occurred with the food handlers regarding proper hand washing/ drying procedures. Frequently review proper hand washing procedures with all employees to prevent the recontamination of clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw meat stored above milk in the kitchen’s double door cooler. CORRECTED- kitchen staff rearranged the raw meat below the milk to reflect proper storage order. Inspector provided the PIC with storage order chart to review with employees, or post on a cooling unit. Ensure animal proteins are always stored below ready to eat (RTE) foods, and animal proteins are stored by increasing cooking temperatures. Items that require the highest internal cooking temperatures should be stored at the bottom of cooling units to prevent the contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) foods to be out of temperature. Milk in the mini fridge on the counter was initially observed at 45F, and multiple desserts in the display cooler were observed to have an ambient temperature between 45-51F. After turning down the cooling units, the following items were observed above 41F: 2 cherry pies (45F internal temperature), 1 chocolate cream pie (45 internal temperature), and 1 cinnamon roll with cream cheese icing (46F). CORRECTED- the food items listed were removed from the cooling unit to be discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are maintained at or below 41F by frequent monitoring of ambient thermometers.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The dessert display cooler and mini fridge at the server station were both observed to have ambient temperatures between 45-51. CORRECTED- units were turned down. Ensure all cold holding units are holding TCS foods at or below 41F. Monitor with ambient thermometers.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: A container of shredded cheese in the walk in cooler was observed without a lid. CORRECTED-a pizza pan was placed over the container. Ensure that all foods are protected from contaminants at all applicable times.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler fan has an accumulation of dust. 
2. The shelves holding the dry storage items between the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer. 
3. The floor under the triple sink. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Food Handler Certificates were unavailable for multiple employees on staff during today’s inspection. Ensure all food service staff obtain a Food Handler’s certificate to be made available during future inspections. Inspector provided guidance on where to find ANSI-approved Food Handler’s certificate Courses.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
No Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPMs) on site during today’s inspection had completed Allergen Training. Inspector provided literature on Allergen training to the PIC. Ensure CFPMs complete Allergen Training, and maintain on file for future inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During this inspection there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts at the facility. It is suggested that the night manager acquire a CFPM moving forward.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

A can is observed in storage with major dents in both the top and bottom seams. The PIC was shown and damage to the packages discussed. The can was separated out for credit to correct. Ensure that all packages are checked as product is received.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several utensils throughout the storage racks in the facility are observed with food residue still evident. The PIC was shown and moved the items back o dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage and use.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A-B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be marked with the date by which it should be used or discarded after opening of the package or preparation in the facility. This date should be 7 days from the date of opening/preparation with the date of preparation/opening counting as day one. 

1) Containers of cheese sauce prepared yesterday and placed into the cooler for cooling are without date marking. Dates were added during this inspection to correct. 2) Individually packaged portions of deli meats are in a container in the bottom of a prep cooler without date marking. The situation was discussed with the PIC and a date marking added to the container to correct.  Ensure that all foods needing date marking are dated appropriately in the facility.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

1) A spray bottle in the kitchen is without a legible label. The PIC indicated that it is water and a label was re-applied to correct. 2) The same type of bottle was observed in the bar area and contains sanitizer. The bar manager was consulted and added a label to correct. Ensure that all chemicals containers are labeled correctly at all times in the facility to ensure that they are not accidentally used for purposes that they were not intended for.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Two containers of cheese sauce int he walk in cooler are observed without lids. The PIC was consulted and added lids to the containers to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are protected from contaminants at all applicable times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

On arrival there is not test strips available for the quat based sanitizer used in the bar area of the facility. The situation was discussed with the bar manager and test strips will need to be acquired prior to the follow up in 10 days.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer bucket available to sanitize food contact surfaces in the kitchen. A Quaternary ammonium sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 400ppm. Ensure that there is always a chemical sanitizer made and available to be able to sanitize food contact surfaces during all hours of food preparation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.

CORRECTED- The eggs were moved below the hashbrowns and the operator was educated on correct storage order. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the bar soda machine to be soiled with mold. The nozzles were removed and properly washed, rinsed and sanitized during the inspection. Remember to manually clean the soda nozzles on a regular basis. 
Also, several small ladles were hanging in the kitchen soiled. Manager stated that he had purchased new and that those were to be discarded. The ladles were discarded immediately. 
Violations are considered corrected on site. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: Inspector observed cans of insect spray stored next to the syrup on a shelf. Aerosol cleaner was observed sitting on the top shelf next to some paper plates. Chemicals and insect sprays were moved to proper storage areas. Take care to keep back storage area organized. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

(A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: Inspector observed that the coffin cooler holding juice at the bar is missing a thermometer. A thermometer was added to the cooler. Ensure that a thermometer is present in this unit and all units that hold temperature control for safety food. The violation is considered corrected on site. 
(A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed bottled juice at the bar to lack date marking. Date mark juice and use within 7 days. Cream pies and meringue topped pies also lack date marking. These pies are cut nightly, placed in the cooler and used at lunch. Any pies left at the end of day shall be date marked. Facility plans to use day dots for pies. Dates were placed on items.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a soda, cigarette lighter, phone and keys on a shelf with gloves and other food related items. Separate personal items from food related items.  

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The magnetic knife holder is observed to be visibly soiled at the start of today’s inspection. PIC removed the items from the magnetic strip and placed them into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. While the items were removed, PIC performed a CIP of the magnetic strip with a sanitizing step before replacing the items to the strip. Ensure this surface is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean to sight and touch. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: The facility was observed to be using reusable cloths when utilizing a spray bottle of sanitizer. Corrective action and education have been given to utilize disposable paper towels when using a spray bottle of sanitizer. A solution has been determined that the sanitizer bucket will be available to store the wiping cloth and then the cloth will be removed form the bucket when in use with a spray bottle. Once finished wiping the surface, the wiping cloth will be placed back into the sanitizer bucket until it is ready to be used again with the spray bottle.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The mop sink is observed to have pulled away from the wall enough to create a visible gap. This gap needs to be resealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket was recorded at 0ppm at the start of the inspection. The bucket was made fresh during the inspection and recorded at a concentration of 200ppm QUAT. Ensure a sanitizer bucket is tested regularly to ensure its concentration remains effective during all hours of operation. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There was a wiping cloth observed stored on the slicing machine. This cloth was removed from this surface and placed into the sanitizer bucket solution during the inspection. Ensure wiping cloths are stored properly when not in use completely submerged in the sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-303.11: There is observed a light bulb burnt out in the hood system. Ensure this light bulb is replaced at the earliest convenience once the casing has cooled down. 
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There were observed two squeeze bottles stored directly in with the lettuce in the sandwich prep cooler. These bottles were removed and placed on the wire shelving in the under part of the cooler. Ensure the food items, especially RTE foods remain protected from contamination during storage.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: The ice scoop was observed to be stored on the top of the ice machine. The scoop was washed, rinsed and sanitized and placed directly into the ice bin. PIC stated they will be placing the scoop into a clean container to store it out of the ice. Ensure the scoop is stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The shelving of the metal shelves under the pizza machine and along the wall are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue. Ensure these shelves are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residues. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Date marking was not observed in the walk-in cooler on the food items within wither prepped or thawed and awaiting prep. Ensure date marking is placed on all required food items within the food establishment where the items shall follow the 7 day date marking rule with day 1 being date of prep and day 7 being the discard date. Date dots are being placed onto the food items during the inspection with the required information based on prep date. 
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Food items were observe din the walk-in cooler without proper date marking. PIC was informed of this violation and informed inspector of prep dates and labeling process. Corrective action is being taken to retrain on date marking and ensuring that day of prep is day 1 and day 7 food items are being discarded.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Spray bottles were observed in three locations containing unidentifiable substances by inspector. During the inspection, PIC was able to identify and label containers of bleach sanitizer and degreaser. Ensure that all bottles being used with unoriginal substances are being labeled for easy identification with the common name of the contained material.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: The sanitizer bucket was unavailable during the start of the inspection. When this issue was brought to the PIC’s attention, a bucket of QUAT sanitizer was immediately made and ready for service. This violation was corrected on site with a concentration on 400ppm QUAT sanitizer.
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The floor under and near the fryer was observed to have an increased accumulation of grease. During the inspection, the equipment was moved and the surfaces were cleaned. Prevention methods were discussed with the PIC which involved placing cardboard down under the side table and switching it out every time it becomes soiled.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-302.12: A non-labeled spray bottle was observed on the kitchen prep shelf. Upon questioning, the cook identified the substance as water that is used to spray on the pretzels to make the salt stick. It was instructed to label the outside of the bottle to display the contents inside. The bottle was labeled with H20 during the inspection. Ensure that all unidentifiable contents in non-original containers are properly labeled with its contents. 
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: The mop head was observed to be stored in the basin of the mop bucket. The mop was moved to where the mop head is able to drip dry in the top of the mop bucket. Ensure this practice continues to limit the growth of potential pathogens and reduce risks of contamination form the mop head.
4-903.11: (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The two compartment sink in the kitchen area by the mop sink was observed to have a slight leak coming from the hot water handle. Ensure this issue is repaired to prevent leaking from taking place.
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.
